item.title: Noah Kahan Latest Musician to Slam White House For Unauthorized Use of His Music in Social Media Hype Clip: ‘Would Never Approve’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news. Today, we're talking about the White House and its use of popular music in social media posts. It seems like another artist has spoken out against the administration for using their song without permission.
[Short music transition]
Host: Noah Kahan, a 29-year-old singer-songwriter, recently took to Instagram to express his frustration. His song "American Cars" was used in a White House post about President Trump's visit to a Michigan auto plant. Kahan commented, "Would never approve of my music being used in support of you or this administration." The song was featured in a TikTok video, but the audio was disabled on Instagram.
[Short music transition]
Host: Kahan's cowriter, Noah Levine, also left a comment, saying, "You fat f–k this song isn’t for you." However, it appears that Levine's comment was removed. The White House has not responded to requests for comment.
[Short music transition]
Host: Kahan is not the only artist to speak out against the White House using their music. Katy Perry, Ariana Grande, and many others, including Beyoncé, Adele, and Rihanna, have all objected to their songs being used in campaign and administration hype videos. It's clear that these artists want to control how their music is used and don't want to be associated with the administration's agenda.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. We'll keep you updated on the latest music news and controversies.
